title: ReadIndexTracker.recordAck stores an unvalidated echoedRound — one voter can fake a freshness quorum for a whole leadership term, serving a stale read as linearizable
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Correction — the fix I prescribed below (`minOf`) is WRONG. The clamp must be a DISCARD.

I wrote `lastAckRound[from] = minOf(echoedRound, round)` below, reasoning by analogy to the
`minOf(m.matchIndex, state.lastLogIndex)` clamp two lines away in the same handler. That analogy is
false, and an adversarial pass demonstrated it **on a branch with the clamp already applied**:

```
forgedEchoArrivingAfterBumpMustNotConfirmRead FAILED
  a forged echoedRound must not count as an answer to round 6 ==> expected: <[]> but was: <[7]>
```

Byte-identical to the pre-fix receipt.

**The mechanism:** `minOf` denies the forger a *permanent* seat but maps the forged value onto the
**most favorable valid one**. A forged `Long.MAX_VALUE` arriving after any `bumpRound()` is credited at
the *current* round — indistinguishable from an honest answer to the round the leader just broadcast and
the forger never answered. Echo MAX on every reply and you keep rolling freshness for the whole term:
the same exploit, re-armed per frame instead of once.

**Why the analogy fails.** `matchIndex` is a **quantity** — clamping to a valid bound is a meaningful,
conservative answer. `echoedRound` is a **nonce**, and `echoedRound > round` is *proof* the leader never
sent that round; there is no conservative interpretation to fall back on. §6.4's property is that the
leader exchanged heartbeats with a majority **after the read arrived**, and `minOf` severs precisely the
request→response causal link the nonce exists to enforce.

**The correct fix:**

```kotlin
if (echoedRound <= round) lastAckRound[from] = echoedRound
```

title: Seam contract does not require collapsing peers before latching Torn, so CompositeSeam's peers fold trusts a convention
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`CompositeSeam.publishPeers` folds a ply's peer set to decide which composite peers are reachable. Its only
liveness test is `live[plyId] != null`, so a ply that has latched `Torn` but is **not yet detached** still
contributes. What stops that being a stale-inclusive `peers` today is a **convention, not the contract**:
every in-tree fabric collapses its roster to `{selfId}` *before* latching `Torn` —
`LinkSeam.kt:166-171`, `MeshSeam.kt:527-530` — so a torn ply contributes an empty set.

That obligation is **not** stated on the `Seam` contract (`Seam.kt:44-56`) and **not** asserted by
`SeamConformanceSuite`. A consumer-authored fabric that tears without collapsing leaves `peers` advertising a
peer reachable only through the torn ply until detach — while `resolveSendTargets` filters it correctly, so
`sendTo` throws `PeerNotConnected` for a peer `peers` calls reachable.

### Why the obvious one-line fix is wrong

Surfaced during #1807 review as "just add `handle.woven &&` to the fold". It is **not** safe as written:
`PlyHandle.woven` is mirrored by the `seam.state` pump, which requests only a **capability** recompute, never
a peers one. So `woven` would become an input to the peers fold with no trigger — a fresh instance of the
lost-trigger defect #1784 exists to close (a ply reaching `Woven` after its peers were mirrored would stay
stale-*exclusive*, permanently). Taking it needs a peers recompute added to the state pump too, which is a
behaviour change the fold's current tests don't cover.

### Proposed

Fix it at the contract, not the consumer:

1. State on `Seam` that a seam must collapse `peers` to `{selfId}` before (or atomically with) latching
   `Torn` — a torn seam has no reachable peers by definition

title: PlyInboundGate's per-origin maps are keyed on a peer-chosen id with no cap on the number of origins
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`kuilt-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/core/composite/PlyInboundGate.kt:16-18`

```kotlin
private val nextExpected = mutableMapOf<PeerId, Long>()
private val buffers = mutableMapOf<PeerId, MutableMap<Long, ByteArray>>()
```

Both are keyed on `frame.originId` — a field the **sending peer chooses**, read straight off the wire by `PlyFrame.decode`. `maxBuffered` (default 16) bounds the buffer *within* one origin; nothing bounds the **number of origins**. `nextExpected` in particular is never pruned: `accept`'s first-sight branch inserts an entry and no path removes it.

So a peer that varies `originId` per frame grows both maps without bound — one `nextExpected` entry plus one `LinkedHashMap` per distinct id, for as long as the ply stays attached. Remote memory exhaustion on a peer-controlled path, no malformed frame required: every frame is well-formed.

## Reachability

Same inbound path #1788/#1809 just hardened, and **marginally more reachable now that the pump survives** a bad frame — which is obviously still the right trade. Pre-existing, not introduced by #1809.

A legitimate composite has one origin per remote composite peer, so the honest working set is small and bounded by the roster. The gap is that nothing enforces the relationship between "origins I have state for" and "peers I have admitted".

## Fix directions

1. **Cap the origin count** and evict LRU (`nextExpected` is already effectively insertion-ordered if switched to `LinkedHashMap`). Cheap, no cross-component coupling, but an eviction re-baselines that origin's sequence — acceptable, since that is what the existing gap-skip already does for liveness.
2. **Gate on membership** — only accept an origin present in `idMap`/`peers`.

title: MeshHello/NwHello decode a nonce of any length while their KDoc declares it fixed — dedup identity is peer-controllable
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Both handshake preambles document an invariant their decoder does not enforce.

`kuilt-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/core/fabric/MeshSeam.kt:85-87` and `kuilt-nw/src/commonMain/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/nw/NwHello.kt:17-19` both say:

> The nonce is raw bytes (not hex-encoded) and **always exactly `NONCE_BYTES` bytes long**.

Both decoders take whatever is left:

```kotlin
val nonce = frame.copyOfRange(4 + idLen, frame.size)
```

`NwHello` is a literal port ("Ported from `:kuilt-core`'s `MeshHello`"), so the gap was copy-propagated rather than independently introduced.

## Why this is more than input policy

`canonicalLinkNonce(a, b)` hex-encodes both nonces, sorts the two strings, and joins them with `:` — that string **is** the link identity mesh dedup agrees on across both endpoints. A peer that sends a **zero-length** nonce contributes `""`. Two distinct misbehaving peers therefore yield the *same* canonical identity, so dedup can collapse or mis-survive links that are genuinely distinct. The value is entirely peer-controlled and reaches the dedup decision with no validation.

Not a crash — #1788/#1809 hardened the length-prefix reads on these same two decoders (short buffer, negative length, overflowing length). This is the field-*width* invariant those left alone, deliberately, as separate from the crash class.

## The tell

`MeshHelloTest.roundTripSingleCharId` encodes a **4-byte** nonce. The repo's own test violates the documented invariant, which is why adding `require(nonce.size == NONCE_BYTES)` fails the suite today. That test is evidence the invariant was never enforced, not evidence that variable-length nonces are wanted.

## Fix

Enforce on **both** decoders (`require(frame.size - 4

title: warp-test: an absorbed budget-overrun retry is invisible, and the reference price is biased toward blaming the host
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Two follow-ups on `retryingOnlyBudgetOverruns` (`:kuilt-warp-test`), landed in #1801. Both are about the *diagnostic*, not the retry — the retry is correct and pinned by five deterministic tests. Part of #1739.

## 1. An absorbed overrun leaves no trace, which is #1739's own thesis one level up

`BudgetOverrunRetry.kt` accumulates each absorbed overrun into a `StringBuilder` that is only ever read on **exhaustion**. So the transition from "0 retries consumed, ever" to "3 of 4 consumed on every run" is completely invisible until the day all four fail — at which point it reads as a fresh regression rather than as drift that had been building for weeks. That is exactly the failure #1739 exists to stop: a signal that silently encodes a machine assumption and only speaks when it is already too late.

It also matters for the one thing the review correctly flagged as **unproven**: the tail *rate*. #1801 showed that **one** attempt suffices at 1-minute load 74, not that **four** are enough there. Emitting absorbed overruns is what would ever tell us the rate had moved.

Fix: emit each absorbed overrun as it happens, via an injected sink rather than a hard-coded `println`, following the established common-code test-support pattern in `MultiNodeRaftSim.kt:544-549` — `emit: (String) -> Unit = { println(it) }`. Gradle captures stdout into the per-test report, so a retry becomes visible in CI without failing anything.

## 2. The reference price is biased toward the comfortable branch

The exhaustion message prices a well-behaved invocation on a fresh runtime and asks the reader to compare it with the budget. Two biases, both inflating the reported cost:

- **It times `load` + `invoke`, not the `invoke` it is compared agai

title: Key the admit fan-out queue by recipient, so one wedged link cannot delay announcements to healthy peers
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Follow-up from the review of #1800 (finding I4). Not a regression once #1800 lands — that PR bounds the hazard — but the bound is loose and the invariant is stronger than it needs to be.

## What #1800 leaves in place

`SeamRoom` sends every host-authoritative membership announcement (`Paused`/`Unpaused`/`Farewell`/roster-sync `Welcome`) through **one** FIFO writer draining `admitFanOuts`. That gives *global* enqueue order == wire order.

The invariant #1781 actually needs is **per-recipient** order: every inversion in that issue, and every one pinned by `AdmitFanOutOrderingTest`, is two frames to the *same* remote. A global FIFO is strictly stronger, and the difference it buys is **head-of-line blocking**: with one writer, a single slow or wedged recipient delays announcements to every healthy peer.

`Seam.sendTo` can suspend for a long time — `LinkSeam`'s outbox is a bounded `BufferOverflow.SUSPEND` channel by design, so a black-holed link (`conn.send` never returns, seam never tears — the #1655 shape) backpressures its caller indefinitely. #1800 caps each send with `withTimeoutOrNull(reconnectWindow + timeout)`, so the wedge is finite rather than permanent, but a wedged peer still costs every healthy peer up to one budget per fan-out.

## Proposed change

Key the queue by `PeerId` — a writer per recipient, or `Map<PeerId, Channel<ByteArray>>` — so a wedged peer stalls only its own stream. That preserves exactly the per-recipient ordering the invariant requires and removes the head-of-line delay entirely, with no duration budget in the ordering path.

Not folded into #1800 because it needs its own lifecycle (create on first fan-out to a recipient, close on evict in `removeFromRoster`, close all in `leave`

title: warp: a post-timeout invoke inherits the dying runaway's queue wait, so its execution budget under-measures
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## The claim that does not hold

`ChicoryWasmRuntime.invokeMutex`'s KDoc says:

> Holding this for the whole submit+get makes the timeout measure actual execution, not queueing: a waiting op gets its full budget from the moment it starts.

True when the previous op **completes**. Not true across a **timeout**. The real `TimedGuestRunner` does:

```kotlin
} catch (e: TimeoutException) {
    future.cancel(true)
    throw e
}
```

`Future.cancel(true)` only sets the worker thread's interrupt flag and returns immediately — Chicory's interpreter observes it at the next call entry / backward branch. The timed-out coroutine then unwinds out of `invokeMutex.withLock`, **releasing the mutex while the worker is still running the cancelled task**. The next op acquires the mutex, submits, and its `future.get(executionTimeout)` clock starts counting *queue wait behind the dying runaway* — exactly the skew the mutex was introduced in #942 to remove, relocated from the completion edge to the timeout edge.

## Why it matters

Normally the residual is microseconds. Under CPU starvation the worker may not be scheduled for hundreds of milliseconds and the innocent op is charged for it. In production a `WarpNode` op invoked right after another op timed out can therefore record a **spurious terminal `WasmExecutionException`** on a perfectly good kernel — and terminal failures are not retried.

Found while fixing #1739's two `:kuilt-warp-runtime` false reds (#1801). Those were fixed at the *assertion* level — the tests now tolerate a transient overrun — so the production skew is untouched and unobserved by any test.

## Why it needs design, not just a grace-wait

The obvious fix is to wait for the cancelled task to actually termin

title: A joiner emits Partitioned twice for its host on a Timeout-then-tear sequence
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found while implementing #1723 (PR #1789) and deliberately reported rather than folded in — it is an
event-stream change, not a level change, so it sits outside that task's scope.

## The duplicate

On a **Timeout-then-tear** sequence a joiner emits `MembershipEvent.Partitioned` for its host
**twice**:

1. the heartbeat detector times out → `markPartitioned` → emits `Partitioned(host)` and writes the level
2. the socket then tears → `runJoinerTornWatcher` → `attemptReconnect` → `onReconnectStarted` → emits
   `Partitioned(host)` **again**

That ordering is the real-hardware one (the radio dies, then the socket notices), so this is a reachable
path rather than a theoretical interleaving.

`markPartitioned` gates its emission on `!wasPartitioned`. `onReconnectStarted` has no such gate — it
did not need one before #1789, because it wrote no level and there was nothing to be idempotent about.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

`Liveness.Partitioned.since`'s KDoc states the deadline agrees with "the single
[MembershipEvent.Partitioned] that was actually emitted (that event fires only on the first
detection)". On this lane that is **no longer strictly true**. The level is still correct — #1789
preserves `since` as first-detection precisely so the level agrees with the *first* event — but the
documented justification now rests on a claim the code does not honour on every lane.

A consumer counting partition events per peer, or treating `Partitioned` as an edge-triggered
"show the reconnecting banner" transition, sees the same partition twice. Nothing breaks; it is
sloppy, and it makes the KDoc's reasoning unsound.

## Suggested fix

Gate the second emission the way `markPartitioned` does — emit only when the host

title: heddle: residue sweep — an under-acked LEAF spend is a real conservation break, not a benign residue (§6.5.2)
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Split out of #1693 (slice 3) as fork 2 — the consequential one. See
`docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §14 item 4.

## What changed

`docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §6.5.2 used to reassure that a post-fence residue was
*"not a conservation break (`rollupSpent` is outside the identity; a leaf-edge residue keeps the
identity true because the spend was real)"*.

The first clause holds. **The second is false.** `holdings` subtracts `effLeafSpent(f)` at the
child's *live inbound* edge, so an under-acked **leaf** spend moves the **credit** onto the live edge
without moving the **charge** with it:

```
Σ holdings + Σ effLeafSpent  >  minted
```

by exactly the under-acked amount. §6.5.2's text has been corrected on the slice-3 PR.

Pinned by `EntitlementLedgerReconcileTest.namedResidual_anUnderAckedLEAFSpendDoesBreakTheIdentityContraDesign652`.

## Severity, honestly

Bounded, and **diagnosed rather than silent**:

- Reachable **only** through the cross-incarnation gap — a peer that acks normally marks the edge
  unwritable and then reads its own slots, so it cannot understate. A restart with an empty local
  ledger can.
- It surfaces as `PerEdgeSafety` on the edge, and the gap is machine-attributable from the log
  (`base(s)[r] > ackedFinal(s)[r]`).

So it is not silent corruption. It is a conservation break that the ledger reports.

## What this issue is for

The **residue sweep** — a second quiesce/ack/derive round moving `base − ackedFinal` through the
reloc counters, iff the live edge's headroom covers it — was specified as a follow-up and
*refused in v1*. Its justification should now be read as **this case is why it exists**, not as an
optional tidy-up. Narrowing the reachability instead (du

title: heddle: Quilter needs a "one full anti-entropy exchange completed" signal (unblocks §6.5.2(a)'s ack narrowing)
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Split out of #1693 (slice 3) as fork 1. See `docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §14 item 3.

## What

`docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §6.5.2(a) specified that a restarted peer replays the
control log **and completes one anti-entropy exchange** before acking a quiesce barrier. The
anti-entropy half is what recovers the peer's own floating write from whichever peer still holds it,
and it is what *narrows* the cross-incarnation ack gap.

It was never implementable as written: there is no `Quilter` primitive that signals **"one full
exchange has completed"** — nothing to wait on. Slice 3 therefore shipped the control-log half only,
and §6.5.2 has been corrected to describe what actually ships.

## Consequence today

The §6.5.2 cross-incarnation residual is **exactly as wide as the design states** when no
anti-entropy has run, rather than narrowed.

⚠ **Corrected 2026-09-06 — this paragraph used to say "nothing is silently wrong".** That is not
true in at least two shapes measured under #2749: an amnesiac re-ack can clear a frozen edge while
silently moving units from recipient to donor with **`validate()` empty**, and a single-declarer
fenced edge can have `Reconcile` refuse with **`nothing stranded`** — the *idempotence* message,
which reads as success — while units really are stranded. So the residue is **not** reliably
surfaced by `PerEdgeSafety` nor attributable via `base > ackedFinal`. See the comment below.

And the case is the default rather than an exotic: `:kuilt-heddle` has **no durable store**, so
every restart looks amnesiac until anti-entropy has run — which is exactly the signal this issue
asks for.

title: refineWindow can move a reconnect deadline backwards across a recover→re-partition cycle
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Status:** this issue had two halves. The **wire-ordering** half is addressed in #1800. What remains — and what this issue now tracks — is the **episode-identity** defect in `refineWindow` below. See #1800 for the half that is done; it needs no further work here.

## What remains: `refineWindow` can move a deadline backwards across a recover→re-partition cycle

`SeamRoom.refineWindow` no-ops unless the member is **currently** `Liveness.Partitioned`. That guard covers "the window announcement arrived after the member recovered, and it is still recovered" — it does **not** cover "recovered, then partitioned again".

A `JoinerReconnectController` emits `JoinerReconnectEvent.WindowOpened` from its own `scope.launch` (see `DefaultJoinerReconnectController.onPeerUnresponsive`), so the event for partition episode *N* can in principle land after episode *N+1* has opened, and move episode *N+1*'s `windowExpiresAt` backwards to episode *N*'s deadline. It bites the default controller too, not only an injected policy (#1614).

**Why it is theoretical:** the recovery→re-detection gap is at least one `HeartbeatConfig.timeout`, orders of magnitude above coroutine launch latency. No observed failure.

**Why the obvious cheap guard was rejected:** `if (expiresAt < current.since) return` looks like it closes this and does not. With a window longer than the recovery→re-detection gap — the controller's 60 s default is — the stale episode's deadline still lands *after* the new episode's `since`, so the guard passes and the level still moves backwards. Shipping it would leave a future reader believing the case is handled.

**Sound fix** needs the detection instant (or an episode sequence number) carried on `JoinerReconnectEvent

title: Precedence tag can permanently capture a transient Available from the composite rollup (one site of four)
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found by an adversarial review of #1773. **Not a regression** — it is a residual of that fix, and
strictly better than what it replaces — but it should be settled before the precedence tag lands
rather than left implicit.

## The residual

#1773 fixes a wedge where `CompositeSeam.capability` stranded on a confident `Available` while every
ply was down, permanently. The fix folds over each ply's **mirrored announced** value instead of a
live read, which closes the strand structurally.

What remains is a **transient**: because a mirrored fold necessarily combines announcements written at
different instants, one may already be superseded at fold time, so the composite can briefly publish
`Available` after both plies have dropped. Self-correction is *guaranteed* (StateFlow's eventual
delivery forces every mirror to the ply's true value at quiescence) but the **latency is not
bounded** — the window is "until the preempted pump is next dispatched", which under CPU starvation
is not microseconds. Measured: 0 transients in 4000 rounds at load 2.42, 1 in 4000 at load 5.13.

The reviewer implemented the obvious alternative (withhold publishing while `mirror != live`, using
the live read only to detect supersession) and it is **worse**: monotone, but a single starved pump
freezes the whole rollup indefinitely *in both directions*, so a peer would fail to notice its network
came back. Generation/version stamps cannot help, because a pump only increments when it *delivers*,
so no stamp reveals an undelivered newer value. So the transient is the right trade in `:kuilt-core`.

title: ReferenceTrainer.step and FedAvgKernelCodec.encodeInput return NaN on an empty batch instead of failing fast
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`ReferenceTrainer.step` divides by the batch size with no guard:

```kotlin
val scale = 2.0 / examples.size.toDouble()
```

With an empty batch that is `2.0 / 0.0 = +Infinity`, and both gradients are `0.0`, so
`Infinity * 0.0 = NaN` and the function returns `[NaN, NaN]` — silently, from a `public`
declaration in a published module. `FedAvgKernelCodec.encodeInput` has the same hole: it
validates `weights.size == DIM` but accepts an empty `examples`, so the wasm kernel
(`fedavg_train.wat`, `f64.div (f64.const 2) (f64.convert_i32_u n)`) produces the same NaN.

This violates the repo's fail-fast rule — invalid state should throw, not produce a
plausible-looking wrong answer. NaN then poisons `FedAvg`: it is not caught by
`FedAvg.contribution`'s `sampleCount > 0` guard when the caller supplies a count from
somewhere other than `examples.size`, and once a NaN weight is in a slot it dominates
`Slot.compareTo` (NaN sorts above every other Double) and propagates through `weights`.

**Not reachable from the shipped demos** — `FedAvgWarpSimTest` and
`FederatedLearningExampleTest` always pass a 3-element batch — but reachable by any
consumer of the public API, which is why it is a defect rather than an unreachable guard.

**Fix:** `require(examples.isNotEmpty())` in both entry points, so the empty batch is
rejected before it can reach either the oracle or the kernel and the two stay equivalent
for every input the API accepts.

Found during the Epic-F polish pass (#1683).

title: heddle: revise the newborn-seat register (§5.2) — the effIssued==0 gate and additive read path are refuted
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Successor to the design pass in PR #1740. **Parked deliberately** — recording what was settled so the next attempt does not re-derive it.

## What is settled

**Fix A (make a newborn a waker, no stored seat) is dead.** `HeddleNode.wakeOffsets` is a per-boot in-memory `HashMap` (`HeddleNode.kt:178`), never replicated or persisted, so under A a restarted or late-joining peer has no seat for any edge — trading a rare unconverged-proposer bug for a **certain** §10.5 lifetime-credit violation on every restart.

The rescue fails too, and instructively: persisting `wakeOffsets` locally cannot help a late joiner (no store holds an observation the peer never made), and *replicating* it requires a multi-writer convergent join — i.e. a per-edge max-register in the ledger. **The rescue collapses into fix B's design class.** So the location argument is confirmed from both directions: the seat must live in a join-convergent replicated position.

## What is refuted

B's *class* is right; the *composition* proposed in #1740 is not. Both findings were **executed** against a model using the real per-slot max-join, on branch [`review/1713-seat-design-adversarial`](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/tree/review/1713-seat-design-adversarial):

- **F1 — the `effIssued == 0` seating gate is stale-readable.** Replicated, but a peer missing only the newborn's own `issued` slots (per-author delta loss, or a one-way partition — both legal under the order-free join) still reads `0` and bumps an already-served edge to the moved front. Since the read path is `ev = seat + committed/w`, the late bump **double-counts**: overshoot is linear in the staleness window, **not** the claimed `q / w_min`. Measured at 20× the bound in a single write.

title: heddle: MintRecord is not bound to a root — merging two bootstraps double-counts every mint
body:
**Status: DECIDED 2026-07-30 — option 2 + option 3.** Full reasoning in the decision comment below. Relabelled `needs-design` → `ready` on 2026-08-12: the design question was answered and only the label was stale, which made this read as unstarted work.

_🤖 Status prepended by Claude on behalf of @keddie._

---

> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Split out of #1642 item 2, which shipped the **documentation** half in #1747 and deliberately
stopped at the wire change.

## The hazard

`MintRecord` carries a holder and an amount. It is **not bound to a root** — `bootstrap(root, …)`
folds `root` only into the generated `MintId` *string*. `EntitlementLedger.holdings` credits
`creditIn = mintedHeldBy(r)` to **any** group with no inbound edge. So `piece`-ing two
independently-bootstrapped ledgers yields two rootless groups, **each credited the whole
`mintedTotal`**, double-counting every mint in the Σ-holdings conservation identity — and
silently: no `validate()` check looks at root cardinality.

Pinned as a known limitation by
`EntitlementLedgerValidateTest.mergingTwoIndependentBootstrapsDoubleCountsMintAtEveryRoot`
(that test asserts the *current* wrong behaviour on purpose; it should flip when this lands).

## The fork

1. **Leave it a caller invariant** — status quo after #1747: documented on the class KDoc, on
   `bootstrap`, and in `heddle-ledger-design.md`. Zero cost, zero enforcement.
2. **Bind `MintRecord` to a root** (`MintRecord(root, holder, amount)`) and make `mintedHeldBy`
   root-scoped. Structural and complete — and a **wire-format change** to a `@Serializable`
   component of a shipped CRDT, so it needs a deliberate call.
3. **Cheap middle ground, no wire change:** a `LedgerConflict.MultipleRoots` report from
   `validate()` when more

title: kuilt-websocket: -Pserver.realnet.tests is never forwarded to the test JVM, so WebSocketPeerLinkRealNetworkTest can never run
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`WebSocketPeerLinkRealNetworkTest` (`:kuilt-websocket`, `jvmTest`) **can never run**. It gates on a system property:

```kotlin
Assume.assumeTrue(
    "Skipped: set -Pserver.realnet.tests=true to run real-network integration tests",
    System.getProperty("server.realnet.tests") == "true",
)
```

…but `kuilt-websocket/build.gradle.kts` has **no `systemProperty` forwarding block**, so a Gradle `-P` property never reaches the test JVM. The message tells you to pass `-Pserver.realnet.tests=true`; passing it changes nothing and the test self-skips anyway.

## The contrast

Both sibling modules that use the same opt-in pattern *do* forward:

- `kuilt-cluster/build.gradle.kts` — `providers.gradleProperty("cluster.realsocket.reconnection.tests")` → `systemProperty(...)`
- `examples/build.gradle.kts` — `systemProperty("warp.fl.ws", ...)`

`:kuilt-websocket` was simply never given the equivalent.

## Why it matters

This is **dead coverage that looks live**. The `-P` flag is documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s build-commands table, the skip message advertises the flag, and the test compiles and reports as skipped — every signal says "opt-in integration test", and none says "unreachable". Anyone who runs the documented command believes they exercised the real-network path and did not.

Found while converting the file's port-probe TOCTOU for #1590 (PR #1744): proving that change against this test required a temporary local forwarder, which was reverted and is **not** in that PR.

## Fix

Mirror `:kuilt-cluster`'s block in `kuilt-websocket/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
val flag = providers.gradleProperty("server.realnet.tests").orNull
if (flag != null) systemProperty("server.realnet.tests", flag)
```

title: Loom.capability() still defaults to a confident roleless Available — the un-audited half of the #1712 floor fix
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found while landing #1712 Track A, which removed the identical defect one layer down.

`Seam.capability`'s interface default used to be a hardcoded roleless `FabricAvailability.Available`. Track A flipped it to `FabricAvailability.Unknown("no live path observer on this fabric")`, because a fabric with no path observer asserting "the network is fine" becomes an authoritative false negative the moment a consumer surfaces it (`Room.localFabric`). Each fabric now declares `reportsLiveCapability` through `SeamCapabilities`, enforced by the conformance suite.

**`Loom.capability()` still has the un-audited version of that same default.** It is the pre-connect surface — the one #1530 introduced so a consuming app could turn a failed connect into actionable guidance ("Bluetooth is off", "can't reach the server") — so a confident `Available` from a `Loom` that has probed nothing is the same shape of lie, on the surface whose *entire purpose* is to be trusted for that guidance.

## Why it is not simply the same fix

The two carry genuinely different meanings, so this needs a moment's design rather than a copy of Track A's patch:

- `Seam.capability` = "can my path carry frames **right now**" — a level that changes as radios and paths change.
- `Loom.capability()` = "is this fabric **attemptable on this runtime**" — closer to a static fact (compiled in, permission granted, radio present).

For some looms `Available` is genuinely correct and static (an in-memory loom really is usable). For others it is a guess (a WebSocket loom that has not probed reachability; a multipeer loom that has not read `CBCentralManager` state). So the fix is probably not a blanket floor flip but a per-loom audit, with `FabricAvailability.Unkno

title: otel-logging: attributeMapper runs before the trace/sampling gate, so a DROP-policy untraced event pays for a discarded mapping
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Follow-up from #1630 / PR #1729, which moved `CaptureConfig.attributeMapper` from the drain coroutine to the synchronous log edge so records carry emit-time attributes.

## The residual

`LogCapture.resolveAtEdge` applies the cheap drop predicate first, so a line below `minLevel` or from one of the exporter's own loggers never pays the mapper:

```kotlin
public fun resolveAtEdge(event: NormalizedLogEvent): NormalizedLogEvent? {
    if (droppedBeforeRecord(event)) return null
    val attributes = runCatchingCancellable { config.attributeMapper(event) }.getOrNull() ?: return null
    return event.copy(activeTrace = resolveTrace(), resolvedAttributes = attributes)
}
```

But the **trace/sampling gate** still runs later, inside `capture()` on the drain. So when a `TraceContextProvider` is wired and `CaptureConfig.untracedPolicy` is `UntracedPolicy.DROP`, an untraced event **pays for a mapping whose result is then thrown away** — on the application's logging thread.

This is documented in `CaptureConfig.attributeMapper`'s KDoc ("it runs before the trace/sampling gate — so a mapper is paid for even when a wired `TraceContextProvider` later drops the event") rather than fixed, because fixing it was out of #1630's scope.

## Why it is worth closing

The whole point of moving the mapper to the edge is that it now runs on the caller's hot logging path. Anyone who wires a provider with `untracedPolicy = DROP` is by definition expecting most events to be discarded — which is exactly the configuration where the wasted work is largest, not smallest.

## Suggested fix

`resolveTrace()` already runs at the edge, so the information needed to apply the untraced policy is in hand there. Move the drop half of the gate into `reso

title: Test-harness class: 293 hand-rolled 5 s real-time runTest budgets are load-sensitive false-red generators
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## The pattern

`runTest(StandardTestDispatcher(), timeout = 5.seconds)` appears **293 times across 92 files in 19
modules**:

```
17 kuilt-session   16 kuilt-warp    15 examples     11 kuilt-game    6 kuilt-core
 6 kuilt-cluster    3 kuilt-warp-runtime            3 kuilt-heddle   2 kuilt-warp-heddle
 2 kuilt-liveness   2 kuilt-conformance             2 demo           1 each: kuilt-warp-test,
kuilt-test, kuilt-raft-test, kuilt-quilter, kuilt-nearby, kuilt-gossip-test, kuilt-gossip
```

(file counts; `grep -c` over occurrences gives 293)

## Why it is wrong in principle

Under `StandardTestDispatcher` with seeded RNG and in-memory transports, a test has **no real-clock
input anywhere in its execution path**. Its virtual trajectory — and therefore the total quantity of
real work it performs — is identical on every run. A wall-clock `timeout` on such a test asserts
nothing about the code; it asserts *"this box can retire N units of work in 5 s"*. That is a
statement about machine load, and it is false exactly when the box is busy.

Measured on #1382 (`BatchedExecutionSimTest`, 16-core box, cache disabled):

| 1-min load avg | test body wall time |
|---|---|
| ~4.6 (near-idle) | 0.435 s |
| ~70 (10 concurrent Gradle daemons + K/N clang) | 1.453 s — **3.34×** |

Its sibling method in the same class degraded 3.47× — a uniform contention slowdown, the signature of
"same work, slower box", not of a hot loop.

## Why it also produces the *worst* diagnostic

When this budget trips, `runTest` throws a bare `UncompletedCoroutinesError` with **no state dump**.
Meanwhile the harnesses that these tests use already carry strictly better, **load-independent**
detectors — e.g. `MultiNodeRaftSim.awaitOrDump`'s `withTimeout(with

title: heddle: §7.3 step 3 promises a diagnostic that HeddlePolicy.pick never emits
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Surfaced while amending §7.2 for #1716 (PR #1730) — pre-existing and orthogonal to that change, so it was left alone there.

`docs/heddle-design.md` §7.3 step 3 says:

> If rounding ever yields no eligible candidate: take the minimum, **emit a diagnostic**, carry on.

`HeddlePolicy.pick` implements the `ifEmpty { minBy }` fallback but **emits nothing** — its own comment describes the branch as "defensive only".

So the spec promises an observable signal that does not exist. If the branch ever fires in production it is silent, which is the worst case for a branch nobody expects to reach: the fallback masks whatever rounding condition produced it.

Either:
- **the code should log** (cheap; matches the repo's diagnostic stance — log identities and state, not sizes, so the parent id and the candidate set are the load-bearing parts), or
- **the spec should drop the clause** if the branch is genuinely unreachable — but then say *why* it is unreachable, since "defensive only" is an assertion the spec does not currently justify.

Prefer the first unless the unreachability argument is solid: a `HeddlePolicy` that is pure and has no logger today is a reason to decide *how*, not whether.

Part of #1602 follow-ups. Related: #1716, #1717 (the same class — a silent branch that is invisible exactly when it matters).

title: build: resolveWasmOpt downloads wasm-opt from github.com with no retry — one DNS blip fails the whole build
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`:kuilt-warp-compiler:resolveWasmOpt` downloads the pinned Binaryen `wasm-opt` archive from `github.com` during the build. The download has **no retry, no timeout, and no mirror**, so a single transient DNS or network blip on a CI runner fails the whole job.

## The code

`kuilt-warp-compiler/build.gradle.kts`, inside `abstract class ResolveWasmOpt`:

```kotlin
private fun downloadTo(url: String, target: File) {
    …
    URI(url).toURL().openStream().use { input -> … }
}
```

Called from:

```kotlin
if (!archive.exists() || sha256(archive) != expectedSha) {
    val url = "https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/releases/download/" + …
    downloadTo(url, archive)
}
```

The SHA-256 pin and the local `downloadDir` cache are both correct and should stay. The gap is purely that the one network call has no resilience around it.

## Observed failure

Publish run [30175612990](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/actions/runs/30175612990) (`48a0d1b6`, 2026-07-25 17:25 ET) failed in **Stage publications to local Maven layout**:

```
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.
* What went wrong:
Execution failed for task ':kuilt-warp-compiler:resolveWasmOpt'.
> java.net.UnknownHostException: github.com
```

3729 actionable tasks, 2998 executed — the whole staging build was thrown away for one failed DNS lookup. It cost a snapshot publish and, transiently, a red `main`.

## Why it matters beyond one flake

- **Every cold `./gradlew build` is exposed**, not just `publish.yml`. CI runners start cold; so does any contributor's first build.
- It is a **flake generator**, and this repo's stance is that a flake is never "just a flake" — the next occurrence costs someone a debugging session for a defect that is not in their cha

body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**A joiner whose host goes silent by `Timeout` gets `Partitioned` with no window and no `expiresAt` — nothing to count down from.**

Found while designing #1712 Track A. Verified against `origin/main` @ `8717f823`.

`reconnectController` is constructed only `if (role == SessionRole.Host && roomId != null)` (`SeamRoom.kt:593`), and `runReconnectEventLoop` launches only when it is non-null (`683`). On a **joiner**:

1. The host goes silent by `Timeout` (not `TransportClosed`), so `handlePeerUnresponsive`'s `hostTransportClose` is false and it routes to `markPartitioned` (`1487`).
2. `markPartitioned` emits `Partitioned` (`1507`).
3. It then calls `reconnectController?.onPeerUnresponsive(...)` — **a no-op against `null`**.
4. `propagatePaused` is gated on `role == SessionRole.Host`, so it is skipped.

**No window is opened and no `WindowOpened` is ever emitted.** The same holds for a joiner observing *another* joiner time out locally on a mesh; only a host-authoritative `AdmitMessage.Paused` (`handlePaused`, `1587-1590`) gives that joiner a deadline.

#1635 proposed routing a joiner's host `Timeout` into `attemptReconnect`, and was closed because it regresses the common case. **This is not that.** Nothing here changes which recovery path runs — `markPartitioned` + detector stays exactly as-is. The ask is only that the episode publish a deadline consumers can render.

## Fix

`markPartitioned` already computes `at + heartbeatConfig.reconnectWindow` one line below for the `Paused` fan-out (`1512`). title: kuilt-session: a joiner never sets its host's Member.liveness — roster contradicts events during a host partition
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**On a joiner, `Room.roster` contradicts `Room.events` for the duration of a host partition.**

Found while designing #1712 Track A. Verified against `origin/main` @ `8717f823`.

`SeamRoom.updateMemberLiveness` is called at lines 785, 1229, 1505, 1525, 1583 and 1605. **None of them is the joiner's host-tear path.** `onReconnectStarted` (`SeamRoom.kt:650-653`) emits `Partitioned(hostId)` + `WindowOpened(hostId)` and mutates no roster state.

So while a joiner is partitioned from its host:

- `events` has said `MembershipEvent.Partitioned(hostId)`
- `roster` still reports that host as `Liveness.Connected`

A consumer following the cookbook's advice — *"`room.roster.value.filter { it.liveness == Liveness.Partitioned }` is the same fact, pull-style"* (`agent-cookbook.md:323`) — gets the wrong answer on the joiner side, and a late subscriber that missed the edge has no way to recover the state at all.

## Fix

`onReconnectStarted` sets `updateMemberLiveness(hostId, Liveness.Partitioned(...))`; the resume path clears it. `hostId` is already in `admittedById` on a joiner — `restoreHostDetector` looks it up there.

The clearing side is subtler than it looks and interacts with #1637 — see that issue's plan amendment (branch `plan/1637-sub-timeout-blip`): the no-op-resume path never receives a `ResumeAck`, so `handleResumeAck` — which is where `updateMemberLiveness(sender, Liveness.Connected)` lives (`1229`) — never runs.

Specced as **D3** in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-local-fabric-vocabulary-design.md` (branch `design/1712-local-fabric`). Part of #1712, part of #1618.

…
_commitIndex.value = idx
```

So a state machine folding `committedFrom` **cannot reach an index that counts withheld entries.** There is no marker for the gap and no way to attribute it locally, which makes the natural freshness check —

```kotlin
val fenced = readIndex()
if (myAppliedIndex < fenced) refuse()   // or wait
```

— unsound: right after an election (which appends a no-op) or a membership change, `myAppliedIndex` sits legitimately below `fenced` **forever**, until some later application entry commits and pulls it past the gap. A gate written that way refuses a legitimate act; a *wait* written that way blocks until unrelated traffic arrives. When the pending act is the only thing the caller wants to do, that is a liveness trap.

This is live: `GovernedHeddleNode.prepareNeutral` needs exactly this check to tell "my view is stale" from "genuinely nothing here" (#1713). It currently ships the comparison and accepts a conservative false refusal, documented, because refusing is safe and freezing a wrong value is not. `RaftNode.awaitRead` carries the same latent hazard for any other consumer.

**A projection-side workaround does not exist here.** On a governed heddle node the control plane's `apply()` advances the projection and publishes to the data-plane sink inside one critical sectio

title: heddle: applyEntry silently drops an undecodable log entry — a schema change would vanish topology acts on replay
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Resolution (2026-07-26): option 1 only — log it. PR #1731.**

`applyEntry` now emits a `warn` naming the **entry index** (plus term and byte length, and the decode failure as the cause) whenever a committed entry does not decode as a `ControlEnvelope`. Control flow is unchanged: the entry is still skipped, and the roster's applied-index advance is untouched. A silent hole is now greppable in the on-device store.

Options 2 (**tag heddle entries**) and 3 (**fail closed on a tagged-but-undecodable entry**) were **deliberately not done** — they need a wire-format decision plus a migration story for already-committed untagged entries, and an availability/safety call. They are **not** dropped: carried forward in #1738. Nothing below is stale; the original analysis stands.

---


`HeddleControlPlane.applyEntry` decodes each committed log entry and **silently drops** anything it cannot decode:

```kotlin
val envelope = runCatchingCancellable {
    Cbor.decodeFromByteArray(ControlEnvelope.serializer(), entry.command)
}.getOrNull()
…
if (envelope == null) return   // a non-heddle entry — no outcome, no projection change
```

For its intended case — a genuine non-heddle entry, e.g. a Raft configuration change — that is correct, and the roster's applied index is still advanced first, so the log prefix stays tracked.

**The hazard is that it cannot distinguish "not mine" from "mine, but no longer decodable."** Governed nodes replay the log from index 1 on every boot, so a `ControlEnvelope`/`ControlCommand` schema change that makes an older entry undecodable would cause those acts to **vanish from the projection** — silent topology loss (a `Prepare` disappears, its edge is never known, its child is never scheduled) rath

title: docs(heddle): amend §7.2 with the front definition #1688 settled — the spec still carries the ambiguity
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Issue #1688 existed because `docs/heddle-design.md` §7.2 says a joiner is seated at "the parent's current virtual time" without saying **which set** defines that front — over all ACTIVE children, or only those actually competing. PR #1700 settles it, with measurements: the front is the weighted mean over the **demanding** candidates, the joiner and any co-joiner excluded by name, a **max**-not-mean fallback when nothing competes, and `null` when nothing survives the exclusion.

**But the spec was not amended.** The settled rule lives only in `HeddlePolicy` KDoc, so §7.2 still carries the ambiguity for the next reader — and for a module whose review protocol is *spec*-conformance (`CLAUDE.md`: audit the changed unit against the spec, treating existing code as unproven), an unamended spec is precisely the trap that produced #1688 in the first place.

Wanted in §7.2 (and §7.3 step 2 where they interact):
- The front is the weighted mean over **demanding** candidates, not all ACTIVE ones — with #1688's finding that the all-ACTIVE mean is wrong in **both** directions (it credits a newborn when a sibling idles behind, and penalises one when a satisfied sibling sits ahead).

title: heddle: the §10.6 clamp is enforced only modulo per-schedule() sampling — a sub-round idle window escapes it multi-peer
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Design §7.2's idle-credit clamp is defined on an **event** — a child "goes from not-demanding to demanding". `HeddleNode.refreshWakeClamps` approximates that event by **sampling** each child's demanding state once per `schedule()` entry and comparing against `demandingObserved`. An idle→demand edge that opens and closes between two samples is never seen, so no clamp fires.

**Single-peer this is exactly right** and deliberately so: the front only advances via *this* peer's own grants, all of which happen after the entry sample, so an idle interval that opens and closes between rounds banks nothing locally.

**The escape is multi-peer.** Peer A samples child C as demanding at round *N*. C idles and re-demands before A's round *N+1*, while peer B's grants advance the siblings' replicated `committedService`. A sees demanding→demanding, no edge, no clamp — and C takes a catch-up burst **out of A's holdings**, having banked an idle interval that §10.6 exists to deny.

**Bounded and partly self-limiting:** the burst is capped by A's holdings and the §8.2 caps, and any peer that *did* observe the idle window clamps independently. It is also consistent with the design's stance that wake offsets are scheduler-local and divergence is tolerated. So this is a real gap in §10.6's enforcement rather than a correctness break — but §10.6 is currently enforced only *modulo sampling*, and that qualifier is not written down anywhere.

Wanted:
- A sentence in `refreshWakeClamps`' KDoc stating that the clamp is sampled per `schedule()` entry, so a sub-round idle window can escape it on a peer whose siblings advance via another peer's grants.
- A decision on whether that is acceptable-by-design (likely) or wants a demand-transitio

title: heddle: wake-offset replacement is non-monotone — a re-wake can refund previously-forfeited idle credit
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`HeddleNode.refreshWakeClamps` stores a wake offset by **replacement**, not by join:

```kotlin
wakeOffsets[edge.record.id] = HeddlePolicy.wakeOffset(front = front, vRaw = …, …)
```

The offset is derived from `front`, which is the weighted mean over the **currently demanding** set — and that mean is **not monotone** across wake cycles. So a later wake can compute a *smaller* offset than the one already stored and hand back credit the clamp previously forfeited.

Concretely (weights 1, `sleeperCredit = 0`): C idles at `vRaw` 0 with a runner at 20 → wakes → offset 20, effective vs 20. C runs to `vRaw` 5 (ev 25) and idles again. Sibling D is demanding at vs 10 but starved — no peer holds delegable entitlement, so D's vs cannot advance. C re-wakes; `front` over `{D}` = 10; new offset `max(0, 10 − 5) = 5`; C's effective vs drops **25 → 10**. C re-enters level with a starved sibling despite 25 units of effective history.

**Bounded, and never a conservation break.** Effective vs can never fall below `vRaw`, so the worst case is the §10.6 clamp degrading toward a no-op — credit is under-forfeited, never negative. That is why this is tracked rather than fixed inline.

The analogous clamp in CFS/EEVDF is monotone: materialized vruntime never decreases. Cheap fix:

```kotlin
wakeOffsets[id] = maxOf(wakeOffsets[id] ?: Rational.ZERO, computed)
```

Needs a test pinning that a re-wake cannot lower an effective vs. Found by design review of #1700. Related: #1695 (the clamp's wiring), #1713 (the seat's structural problem, same family of "a derived value that should not be freely rewritten").

title: Liveness vocabulary has no self-attribution: a peer cannot learn that IT is the one offline (2-peer case is undecidable from peer events)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Request: a transport-agnostic *self*-reachability signal in the liveness/presence vocabulary.**

Consumers can currently learn that *some other peer* went quiet, but never that **they themselves** went offline — so a device that loses its own network attributes the outage to its peers.

> **Design landed 2026-07-26:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-local-fabric-vocabulary-design.md` (branch `design/1712-local-fabric`), as Track A of the liveness/readiness area. It also covers #1618 Q2 and two defects found while designing. The **"where the fact lives"** section of this body was wrong; it is corrected below.

## Why this can't be inferred

Per the cookbook: *"Every `PartitionEvent` names a `peerId`."* Every liveness event is about someone else, and `MembershipEvent.Partitioned` / `WindowOpened` / `HostLost` are all peer-attributed.

**In a 2-peer session that makes the two cases indistinguishable.** "The only other peer went silent" is identical whether *they* dropped or *I* did — both sides observe exactly the same event stream. There is no peer-side observation that disambiguates it, so a consumer rendering presence from the vocabulary alone will always be able to say "the other player is disconnected" and never "you are disconnected". With >2 peers you could heuristically infer self-loss from *all* peers going quiet at once, but at 2 peers even that degenerates.

## Where the fact actually lives (corrected)

This body originally said the signal "sits in the **transport**, not in the presence vocabulary" and "exists only for the `nw` lane." Both are inaccurate, and the difference changes the fix:

title: kuilt-nw: browse `add` before TXT resolves — the loom dials on a fallback identity that may be self (late-TXT race)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**The failing test already exists and is `@Ignore`d**: `NwTxtFidelityTest.anEndpointWhoseTxtHasNotResolvedYetIsNotDialled` (landed in #1707). It asserts behaviour production does not implement — enabling it is the acceptance criterion.

## The race

Network.framework can deliver a browse `add` **before** the endpoint's TXT record resolves, supplying identity on a later update. `RealNwApi.onBrowseResult` handles the unresolved case with the documented `readPeerIdFromTxt() ?: name` fallback, so in that window `NwEndpoint.id` is the **`serviceName`**.

Under `Rendezvous.New` every peer — including this one — advertises the *same* shared session name. So for as long as TXT takes to resolve, a self endpoint and a real peer are the same string, `NwLoom.onEndpointFound`'s pre-dial self-filter (`endpoint.id == selfId || endpoint.serviceName == selfId`) cannot fire, and the loom dials its own endpoint. The `NwSeam` post-connect guard catches it, but only after a full connect — which is the #1660 root-1 symptom the TXT opt-in (#1673) was supposed to remove.

**This is the leading explanation for #1673's unresolved run-to-run variance:** functionally identical builds gave 4/4 self-dials in one hardware formation and 0/0 in the next. A race whose window is "however long TXT takes to resolve" produces exactly that signature.

## Why the fallback can't simply be deleted

`id = serviceName` is load-bearing under `Rendezvous.Existing`, where a peer advertises its own `selfId` as the serviceName — there the fallback id *is* a real per-peer identity and dialling on it is correct. title: FakeNwRadio models TXT delivery as always-succeeding — opt-in, absent, late, and name-collision cases untested
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

`FakeNwRadio` models Bonjour TXT delivery as **always succeeding**. Two real defects in the #1660 root-1 fix passed every in-harness test and were only caught by a hardware cycle.

**What the fake missed.** `RealNwApi.startBrowsing` never called `nw_browse_descriptor_set_include_txt_record`. Apple's default is *not* to query TXT (`browse_descriptor.h`: "by default, the browser will not automatically query for TXT records"), so the advertised PeerId never arrived, every endpoint fell back to `id = serviceName`, and under `Rendezvous.New` the pre-dial self-filter could never fire. Fixed in `0f1820f4`; hardware then showed the filter firing and self-dials going 4/4 → 0 (evidence in #1673).

The fake couldn't see it because it has no notion of the browser's TXT opt-in — it just hands over a `peerId` because `markListening` was given one.

**Essential cases absent from the harness:**

- [ ] **TXT delivery gated on opt-in.** The fake should deliver a TXT PeerId *only* if the browse descriptor requested TXT. Without this, forgetting the opt-in is untestable — exactly the shipped bug.
- [ ] **TXT absent / malformed.** `onBrowseResult` has a documented `?: name` fallback that no test drives.
- [ ] **TXT late (add-then-update).** Network.framework can deliver the browse `add` before TXT resolves and supply it on a later update. If we dial on the add, we dial before the id is known — a live self-dial race. Suspected cause of run-to-run variance observed on hardware (identical code gave 4/4 self-dials in one run, 0/0 in the next).
- [ ] **Bonjour name collision / rename.** Under `Rendezvous.New` both peers advertise the same service name and mDNS disambiguates — hardware showed `fireworks-quickplay` and `fireworks-quickp

title: Tigris: objects that HEAD successfully are absent from ListObjectsV2 (silently corrupts any listing-based tooling)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found while investigating #1702. Objects exist in the Tigris bucket that **no listing ever returns**.

## Repro

`0.7.0-dev.945` was published by a green run (#945 logged `=== publishing version 0.7.0-dev.945 (8980 files) ===`). The object is there:

```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket buildcache \
    --key maven/us/tractat/kuilt/kuilt-core-jvm/0.7.0-dev.945/kuilt-core-jvm-0.7.0-dev.945.pom
{ "size": 2380, "modified": "2026-07-25T01:59:48+00:00" }
```

But it appears in no listing, stably across three attempts:

```
$ aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket buildcache \
    --prefix maven/us/tractat/kuilt/kuilt-core-jvm/ --delimiter /
732 CommonPrefixes, contains-dev.945 = 0     (x3)

$ aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket buildcache \
    --prefix maven/us/tractat/kuilt/kuilt-core-jvm/0.7.0-dev.945/
Contents: null
```

Sixteen hours after upload and stable on repeat, so this is not an eventual-consistency window.

## Why it matters

- **Resolution is unaffected** — Gradle GETs an exact URL, which is why fireworks-compose's `validate/3789-both` branch resolves its `0.7.0-dev.945` pin despite the version being unlistable.
- **Every listing-based inventory undercounts.** The measured 124,300 version dirs / ~3.1M objects behind #1702 is a *floor*, not a count.
- **Unlistable objects are unreclaimable** by any enumerate-then-delete tool — you cannot delete what you cannot enumerate. This is a large part of why an S3 **lifecycle rule** (server-side, retroactive, no listing) is the right cleanup mechanism here and a hand-rolled prune job is not.
- It cost real diagnostic time: `dev.945` looked like a green run that silently published nothing, which is a much more alarming hypothesis than the truth.

## Ask

Worth raisin

title: heddle §10.6 wake clamp is unenforced — wakeOffset has no production caller
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Surfaced while investigating #1688. **§10.6's wake clamp is not enforced anywhere in the shipped node** — it exists as a pure function with no production caller.

Evidence (`origin/main`):
- `HeddlePolicy.wakeOffset` (`HeddlePolicy.kt:158`) is referenced **only** by its own KDoc, `HeddlePolicyTest.kt:189`, and a throwaway investigation harness. No production call site.
- `PolicyEdge.virtualOffset` (`HeddlePolicy.kt:25`) defaults to `Rational.ZERO`, and **no production site ever sets it** — `pickOne` constructs every edge with the default. It is read once, at `HeddlePolicy.kt:165`.
- No wake state exists in `HeddleNode` or `HeddleConfig` at all, so there is nothing that could detect the idle→demand edge the clamp is defined on.

**Consequence.** §10.6 exists to stop a child that idled from banking credit and then spending it in a burst on wake. Today a waking child re-enters with its stale (low) virtual service and no forward clamp, so it *does* take a burst of consecutive grants — precisely the behaviour the invariant forbids. `HeddlePolicy` itself is correct; the node never asks it the question.

Measured in the #1688 harness: with `front` supplied correctly, a waker is clamped as designed; with no clamp at all (today's shipped path) it banks the idle interval outright.

**Why this is filed separately from #1688.** #1688 asks *which set* defines `front`. This issue is that there is no production `front` at all. They are a pair — creation-time `V` (#1688) and the wake clamp are the two places the same "seat at the front of the competing set" rule must be applied — and #1688's answer should land together with an actual caller, or it fixes a function nobody invokes.

title: heddle #1665 slice 3 — the quiesce/ack fence + through-service un-gate
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Slice 3 of 3** for #1665 — the fence itself, and the only slice that un-gates through-service. Design: `docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §6.2–§6.5 (PR #1690). **Depends on slice 2 (log-known roster).**

## Scope
- `Quiesce(s)` — committed, gated on RETIRED in log order.
- Each peer, on applying it, **atomically with its own mutator execution**, marks `s` locally unwritable (future `spendCaptured` re-homes to the live lineage; `delegate`/`release` refuse) and proposes `QuiesceAck(s, r, finals)` declaring its own authored slot values, final by single-writer. **The step-2 lock obligation is load-bearing** — the design's own adversarial pass found the barrier-vs-completion race is defeated *only* by it.
- **Apply-derived `Reconcile`**: the magnitude is computed at apply time from log-recorded acked finals. The proposer sends **no magnitudes**. This is what makes the magnitude a deterministic function of the log prefix.
- The **boot-ordering invariant** (§6.5), then — and only then — the through-service un-gate.
- Route the **non-through** path through the same fence, retiring #1669's "not a safety fence — magnitudes read from this possibly stale view" caveat instead of carrying it forever.

## Known limits — implement to these, don't quietly exceed them
- **Named residual §6.5.2**, the one interleaving the design could not defeat: peer charges `s`, delta escapes to exactly one other peer, crash before ack, restart re-acks lower before anti-entropy recovers the floating write. Full closure needs durable per-peer authored-slot storage, deliberately not smuggled in. The residue is **machine-attributable** (`base > ackedFinal` in log state); a residue sweep is specified and **refused in v1**.

title: heddle #1665 slice 2 — log-known roster (Enroll/Depart) for the control plane
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Slice 2 of 3** for #1665. Design: `docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §6.2 (PR #1690).

## The gap
The redesigned fence requires knowing **exactly which peers must acknowledge a barrier**. `grep` confirms **zero** occurrences of `Enroll`/`Depart` anywhere in `kuilt-heddle` today — the control plane has no roster concept at all; it reaches for voter quorum via `RaftNode.readIndex` and otherwise derives membership from the seam, which is **open**. So "every enrolled peer has acked" is currently **undefined**, and no fence can be built on it.

## Scope
A **log-known roster** for the heddle control plane: `Enroll` / `Depart` as Raft-committed control commands, with membership as a deterministic function of the log prefix — the same log-purity property H5's BLOCKER-1 established for the rest of the control state (apply must be a deterministic function of the log, Raft §5.4.3; a gossip-merged view is not admissible).

**Independently reviewable — nothing relocates in this slice.** No fence, no quiesce, no relocation behavior change.

## Design questions to surface rather than guess
- Relationship between the heddle roster and the underlying Raft voter set / seam roster — mirror, subset, or independent? They can legitimately differ.
- What `Depart` means for a peer holding **unreplicated reservations**. This is the boundary of the unshipped `RevocationSeam`; if it can't be answered here, say so and scope `Depart` to the clean case.
- Enrollment of a joiner **mid-fence** (design §6.2 handles this with a commit-index quantifier + boot gate — implement to that).

## Acceptance
- Roster is a deterministic function of the log prefix; two peers applying the same prefix agree.
- Multi-node tests through the canonic

title: heddle #1665 slice 1 — relocation counters (A) + finding-1 witness migration (no fence dependency)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Slice 1 of 3** for #1665. Design: `docs/heddle-ledger-relocation-design.md` §7 (PR #1690). **No fence dependency — ships first, alone, safely.**

## Scope
1. Land the three **relocation counter families** — representation (A). `effective = base + relocIn − relocOut`, two grow-only counters, net decrease without a decrement; join laws inherited by the same `LatticeProduct` argument (design §3, §5.1).
2. `GovernedHeddleNode.reconcile` keeps **REFUSING** `spent(s) != 0` — fail-closed, exactly as #1669 does today. Nothing un-gates in this slice.
3. **Migrate #1669's non-through witness off the contested base-`issued(t)` write onto `issuedReloc.in(t)`** (design §6.3).

## Why part 3 is not optional polish
Finding 1 of the adversarial review attacks the net-inflow re-home half that **#1669 already implements**, so it is *inherited*, not introduced by (A). On that branch:

```kotlin
issuedTarget = issuedTarget.piece(GCounter.of(r to checkedAdd(slot(issued, liveEdge, r), add)))
```

`t` is the **live** edge, which replica `r` writes concurrently via ordinary `delegate` — two writers, one `GCounter` slot, per-slot max-join, one side silently erased. Conservation still holds and per-edge safety still passes, so **nothing surfaces**; units just sit at the wrong node. Slice 1 is therefore a strict safety improvement to the currently-proposed path, independent of everything else.

**#1669 is gated on exactly this** (see its DO-NOT-MERGE comment) — this slice is what un-gates it.

## Hard constraint
**Never ship relocation-enabled `reconcileStranded` ungated.** (A) without the §6 fence is a net safety *regression*: today through-service fails closed; (A) unfenced flips it to silently accepting a relocation of the wrong m

title: heddle — expose the parent's current virtual time V, and settle which edge set defines it at creation time
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Fallout from #1646 / #1687, deliberately left out of scope there.

#1687 gives `V → initialVirtualTime` a single documented rule (`AttachmentRecord.neutralInitialVirtualTime(V) = ⌈V⌉`). But a caller creating a generation at runtime has **no supported way to obtain `V`**:

- `HeddlePolicy.weightedMeanVirtualTime` is `private`.
- It is defined over the per-round **candidate** set (edges with positive `additionalNeed`), per design §7.3 step 2 — which is a *scheduling* notion, not obviously the right notion of "the parent's current virtual time" for **creation** (§7.2/§5.3), where the natural set is arguably the parent's ACTIVE children regardless of demand.

Today every `AttachmentRecord` in the tree is built with the literal `0L`, so nothing is wrong yet — this bites the moment a generation is created under a parent that has already run.

Two questions to settle before exposing anything:

1. Which edge set defines `V` at creation — demanding candidates, or all ACTIVE children? They differ whenever a sibling is idle, and the choice changes where a newborn is seated.
2. What is the public shape — `HeddlePolicy.parentVirtualTime(edges)`, something on `HeddleNode` that reads the ledger directly, or a `HeddleNode.prepareNeutral(...)` that computes and records in one act?

Note the interaction with §7.2's wake clamp: `wakeOffset` already takes a `front` argument with the same ambiguity, and its only caller today is a test that passes a single sibling's `virtualService()`. Whatever answer 1 gets should apply to both.

Part of #1602.

title: warp F3 — secure aggregation for federated learning (deferred from Epic F)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Deferred from Epic F (#856), which closed on the F4 end-to-end demo (#957/PR #1671). F4 proves data-local federated learning (each device trains on its own data; only the 24-byte model header travels) with a leader-failover resilience proof — but the **model updates themselves are sent in the clear**. F3 adds **secure aggregation** so the coordinator/relay learns only the *aggregate* model update, not any individual device's contribution.

Scope (design first): pick a secure-aggregation scheme (pairwise-masking à la Bonawitz et al., or a lighter additive-masking variant over the existing `FedAvg` reduce), decide how masks are agreed (the existing `:kuilt-deal` commit-reveal / SRA primitives may compose here), and how dropout is handled (a device leaving mid-round must not corrupt the aggregate). Compose with the data-local `enqueueLocal` path F4 established.

Not scheduled; `needs-design`. Part of the warp epic (#857).

title: kuilt-crdt: EphemeralMapTracker evict-on-read can re-stamp a stale re-delivered frame as live (author-fresh-delta contract + identical-re-delivery guard)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Follow-up from the #1666 fix (PR #1672, which is net-positive and merged). The fable gate confirmed the fix works but found that `EphemeralMapTracker.received()` evict-on-read accepts **any** inbound entry for an expired slot as fresh — it cannot distinguish a restart's genuine heartbeat from a stale **relay** of the dead incarnation's own frame. Reproduced by execution:

1. **Zombie resurrection** — a crashed, never-restarted peer's identical stale entry, re-delivered after TTL (the anti-entropy / full-state-relay pattern), is re-stamped live for another full TTL, indefinitely on each re-delivery.
2. **`leave()` suppression defeated** — a departed peer's tombstone (@clock 101) is evicted and a laggard's stale presence (@clock 100) reinstalled fresh; the departure guarantee becomes TTL-bounded, not permanent.
3. **"Bounded by one TTL" overstated** — repeated post-expiry stale re-deliveries mask a restart cycle after cycle (probabilistic, not bounded); a full-state exchange holding the dead value regresses an already-recovered observer.

**Reachable in a shipped consumer — fireworks-compose** ([comment](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/issues/1675#issuecomment-5078856926), [execution proof](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/issues/1675#issuecomment-5078883998)). title: warp: WarpNode.enqueueLocal drops lane→ROOT and affinity→Anywhere (pinned task can't carry H6 lane / H8 affinity)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found by the F4 consistency pass (pre-existing on `main`, not introduced by #1671). `WarpNode.enqueueLocal` (`kuilt-warp/src/commonMain/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/warp/WarpNode.kt:~615`) rebuilds the descriptor with only `op`/`args`/`traceparent`/`pinnedOwner`, **silently resetting `lane` → `Lane.ROOT` and `affinity` → `Affinity.Anywhere`**. So a task pinned via `enqueueLocal` can never carry an H6 fair-share **lane** (heddle admission keys on it) or an H8 **affinity** predicate — the two get dropped on the floor for exactly the node-local-pin path that federated-learning / data-local workloads use.

**Fix:** preserve `lane` and `affinity` from the source descriptor when rebuilding in `enqueueLocal` (carry all opaque envelope fields through the pin, not just op/args). Add a test asserting a pinned task retains its lane + affinity.

Part of the warp epic (#857).

title: kuilt-crdt: EphemeralMapTracker never evicts expired entries → restarted replica invisible past TTL (breaks EphemeralMap restart-recovery contract; heddle demand + capability boards)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found (execution-reproduced) by the #1602 capstone; **pre-existing kuilt-crdt bug the heddle epic made load-bearing twice.** `EphemeralMap` KDoc (`kuilt-crdt/.../EphemeralMap.kt:79-91`) promises TTL-bounded restart recovery ("after TTL the slot is cleared and the next heartbeat from the restarted replica is accepted as fresh"). `EphemeralMapTracker.received()` (`EphemeralMapTracker.kt:44-53`) instead compares inbound clocks against the merged `state`, which **never evicts expired entries** — a restarted replica (process-local clock from 0) stays invisible until its counter numerically exceeds the dead incarnation's (verified: 20 heartbeats over 40s vs a 1s TTL, never visible).

Both epic consumers sit on it with clocks-from-zero: `HeddleNode.demandClock` (`HeddleNode.kt:142`) and `WarpNode.capabilityClock` (`WarpNode.kt:370`). After any peer restart: (a) its lanes' demand is invisible to pre-restart peers → delegation starvation; (b) the capability view diverges **permanently** pre/post-restart → divergent `eligiblePeers` → divergent ring owners → duplicate-execution windows (breaks §14.6 determinism). H5 solved the analogous restart-freshness problem for requestKeys via an injected `incarnation`; the ephemeral clocks got no equivalent. **Fix:** evict-on-read past TTL in the tracker, or an injected incarnation/epoch for the clock. Shared CRDT → gate the fix.

Part of #1602.

title: heddle: raced advisory-retire + legal reparent leaves permanent PersistentNegativeHoldings/PerEdgeSafety (poisons validate() semantics, §10.3)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found (execution-reproduced, seed 177 + deterministic repro) by the #1602 capstone. The advisory-retire race documented at `GovernedHeddleNode.retire` (`HeddleGoverned.kt:196-204`) claims a missed race "never drives holdings negative, quarantines the lineage, or breaks deterministic apply" — **false once the raced child is legally reparented:**

1. mint 10→p3; `e1: root→g`, `e2: g→h` active; p3 delegates 10↓e1, 6↓e2.
2. `close(e1)`; a gossip-lagged peer proposes `retire(e1)` (its view shows `outstanding(e1)=0` — the documented race); projection gate (CLOSING) passes.
3. Reparent: `prepare(e3: root→g)`+`activate(e3)` — passes the dual-inbound gate (e1 is RETIRED, not live).
4. Converged: `holdings(g,p3) = −6` → **permanent `PersistentNegativeHoldings(g,p3)` on every peer**, plus the surviving +6 at `h` is spendable via `[e3,e2]` → `PerEdgeSafety(e3)` (`issued=0, spent=6`) — **§10.3 broken permanently, with ZERO actual overspend.** Unclearable (`release` is not exposed on the node).

No inflation occurs (conservation holds), but §4.6 / `validate()` define these exact conflicts as "the real overspend signal" — so operator alerting on them gets an unhealable false alarm. **Fix direction (needs a call):** refuse reparent of a stranded child while a `ClosureViolation` is outstanding, OR reclassify these post-race states in the docs + `validate()`. Consensus-semantics-adjacent → gate the fix.

Part of #1602.

title: heddle: GovernedHeddleNode cannot be wired into warp lane admission (compile hole; KDoc claims it can)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Found by the whole-epic (#1602) capstone review. `HeddleAdmissionControl(private val heddle: HeddleNode)` (`kuilt-warp-heddle/.../HeddleAdmissionControl.kt:53-54`) takes a concrete `HeddleNode`, and its KDoc (:41) advertises "a `heddleStatic` node (no consensus) **or an H5 governed node**." But `GovernedHeddleNode` holds `private val node: HeddleNode` (`HeddleGoverned.kt:117`) with no accessor and no shared interface — so `HeddleAdmissionControl(governed)` fails to compile (`GovernedHeddleNode` is not a `HeddleNode`). The consensus-governed-fair-share-gating-warp-lanes composition is unbuildable as shipped; the ungoverned `heddleStatic`+lanes path works fine.

**Fix (trivial):** extract a data-plane interface (`reserve`/`complete`/`schedule`/`advertise`) that both `HeddleNode` and `GovernedHeddleNode` satisfy, or expose the underlying node, or overload the adapter. Per-phase review missed it because nothing in `kuilt-warp-heddle` references the governed type. Also (follow-on, latent): once wired, namespace the shared-RaftNode `requestId` — control plane uses `seq` and warp uses `taskId.hashCode()` under one `clientId`, a collision space.

Part of #1602.

title: log capture: session-scoped logger context (MDC-equivalent) so attributes aren't process-global
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Ask
A way to bind attributes to a **scope** (a coroutine context / a session), so `CaptureConfig.attributeMapper` (or an equivalent) resolves them **per-emitter** rather than reading process-global mutable state. Essentially an SLF4J-MDC equivalent for kuilt's log capture, ideally coroutine-context-propagated.

## Why
In `tractat-us/fireworks-compose` (ADR-073, consumer issue tractat-us/fireworks-compose#3774) we stamp `game.id` / `session.id` onto `LogRecord`s while a server-mediated game is active. The only hook available today is a single mapper installed on the **whole process's** capture edge, and our runtime holds **concurrent sessions**. So a record emitted by session B is stamped with session A's attributes whenever A is the currently-armed one — the stamp is a process-wide time window, not per-session routing.

For us that is a correctness *and* privacy boundary: a mesh/offline session running alongside an armed server game gets stamped with the server game's `game.id`, and a downstream filter that selects by `game.id` would then treat those records as belonging to the server game. We can't fix it consumer-side — the process-global mapper has no idea which session emitted a given record.

## Shape that would solve it
Any of:
- A `withLogContext(attributes) { … }` that binds attributes to the current coroutine context and merges them at emit time, MDC-style.
- A per-`LogCapture`/per-session attribute source instead of one global mapper.
- Emit-time resolution of a context-scoped attribute bag (this also subsumes the drain-vs-edge timing problem tracked in #1630 — resolving at the edge from a scoped context fixes both).

## Related
- #1630 — `attributeMapper` resolves on the drain coroutine, not t

> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

The genuine remaining #1618 Track B gap, split out after the B.5 "route Timeout into the resume machine" approach was found to regress the common case (see #1635 / #1654).

## What already works (do NOT re-solve)
A joiner whose host goes silent by heartbeat `Timeout` while the seam **self-heals** (`Woven → Weaving → Woven`, or a genuinely-live seam whose frames simply pause and resume) already recovers correctly via `markPartitioned` + `HeartbeatPartitionDetector`: transient → `Recovered` (`Partitioned(LinkTimeout)`), sustained → `HostLost(WindowExpired)`, no re-weave, no leak. Pinned by `JoinerHostTimeoutRecoveryTest` (#1654).

## The gap
A **black-holed / non-self-healing** transport: the host is silent, the connection is wedged `ready`/`Woven` (half-open TCP/WS, an NW connection stuck with no path event), frames never resume on it, and the seam never goes `Torn` (on NW it sits `Weaving` up to ~213 s; in a ≥3-peer room it never even leaves `Woven` — `NwSeam.evictPeerLocked` only re-forms when the registry empties). Here the only recovery is a **fresh dial + `resume(token)`**, which today's `Timeout` path never attempts — it limps to `HostLost` even when reweave would have recovered the session.

## Why it's hard (needs-design)
- **`adopt`-rooms have `reweave == null`** (`SeamRoom.adopt`, ~L182). The NW P2P production path can't reweave at all today — that capability has to be added first (cf. #1632's `reweave={seam}` idea as a building block).
- **The two modes are opposite.** Self-heal wants *passive await + detector Recovered* (silence the resume machine); black-hole wants *active reweave + resume*. The same `Timeout` entry can't naively pick one — needs an explicit **escalation model** (passive-await fir
