title: heddle — HeddleNode lost-then-rejoined peer is never re-monitored (v1 add-only reconcileDetectors)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Flagged by the H4 (#1607) review. `HeddleNode.reconcileDetectors` is **add-only**: it never removes a detector after `PeerLost`, and nothing clears a peer from `_unreachable` except `PeerRecovered`. A peer declared Lost (channel closed, detector loop returned) that later reappears in `peersFlow` gets **no fresh detector** and stays in `unreachable` forever.

**Deliberate for v1** — consistent with design §8.1/§9 ("no reclamation; recovery is a later feature") and the fixed-roster posture; it is marked as intentional in the `reconcileDetectors` KDoc. Not a bug in H4.

**Belongs with the control plane (H5, #1608)** — richer rejoin/recovery (re-attaching a detector, clearing `unreachable`, reclaiming stranded earmarks) is control-plane membership work, not node-local. Track it here so the add-only behavior isn't later mistaken for working reconnection.

Part of #1602.

title: heddle hardening — @Serializable on Rational/Weight bypasses the validating of() factory on the read path
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Surfaced by the H3 (#1606) post-merge review. Both `Rational` (`kuilt-heddle/.../Rational.kt`) and `Weight` (`.../Weight.kt`) are `@Serializable class` whose **only** invariant-enforcing construction path is a private-constructor `of()` factory (reduce to lowest terms, denominator `> 0`). The plugin-generated serializer deserializes straight into the primary constructor, **bypassing `of()`** — so a wire/persisted `Rational(2, 4)` or `Rational(1, -2)` (or a negative-denominator `Weight`) survives unreduced / sign-denormalized. Then structural `equals` and cross-multiplication `compareTo` (which assume a positive denominator) give **wrong answers**, breaking the exact-ordering invariant the module is built on.

**`Rational`: currently unreachable** — it appears only inside `PolicyEdge.virtualOffset`, and `PolicyEdge`/`Grant`/`PolicyConfig` are not `@Serializable`; `virtualOffset` is explicitly non-replicated (§7.2). Fix: **drop the unused `@Serializable`** (YAGNI), or if H4+ intends to replicate a virtual time, add a custom serializer routing through `of()`.

**`Weight`: reachable and higher-value** — `Weight` **is** replicated inside `AttachmentRecord` (topology). A corrupt or hostile peer could inject a negative-denominator `Weight` and **flip sibling ordering** cluster-wide. Fix: custom serializer (or `init`-block validation) enforcing the `of()` invariant on the read path.

Pre-existing from H1 for `Weight`; the H3 review just made the class visible. Companion to the ledger-hardening bucket #1642.

Part of #1602.

title: heddle H4 — define a deterministic V→initialVirtualTime rounding rule (ceil, to preserve §10.5 no-idle-credit)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Surfaced by the H3 (#1606) post-merge review. **H3 itself is correct and safe** — `HeddlePolicy` never creates a record; it reads `AttachmentRecord.initialVirtualTime` (a `Long`) and lifts it exactly.

**The gap is at attachment-creation time, which H4 wires.** §7.2/§10.5 require a newborn generation's `initialVirtualTime` to equal the parent's *current* virtual time `V`. But `V = Σ w·ev / Σ w` is a `Rational` and almost always fractional (e.g. `30/7`), while `AttachmentRecord.initialVirtualTime` is a `Long` — so creation must round, and the direction has a fairness sign:

- **floor** places the newborn slightly in the past → a sliver of lifetime/head-start credit — exactly what §10.5 forbids.
- **ceil** is conservative and invariant-preserving (never a head start).

Concrete bite: once H4 creates generations at fractional `V`, a subtree churning generations accrues a systematic floor-rounding bias, each newborn marginally ahead of siblings. H3's tests cannot see it — they only create at integral `V` (e.g. `neutralCreationGivesNoHeadStart` uses `V = 30/1`).

**Action (H4):**
1. Define one documented, deterministic rounding rule for `V → initialVirtualTime`. **Recommend `ceil`.**
2. Add a neutral-creation test at a genuinely fractional `V` (not integral) asserting no head start.

Record creation is a single recorded act (§9), computed once and replicated, so cross-replica divergence is not the risk — only the fairness direction is.

Part of #1602.

title: kuilt-otel-logging: LogCapture drops ALL us.tractat.kuilt.* logs (self-exclusion prefix too broad — should be us.tractat.kuilt.otel)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Symptom
On iOS, **kuilt's own `KotlinLogging` output never reaches a consumer's capture store** if the logger was created before the (typically async) `installLogCapture` call. A 2-phone hardware capture of a live game found **0** `us.tractat.kuilt.*` lines in the app's otel store — only the app's own loggers (which first logged *after* the swap) were captured. This silently blinded the entire #1618 investigation (and the original reporter's capture) to the kuilt session/liveness/raft layer.

## Root cause (ordering race, not a filter)
`installLogCapture` (`kuilt-otel-logging/.../InstallLogCapture.kt:85-89`) does two process-global mutations: `KotlinLoggingConfiguration.loggerFactory = DirectLoggerFactory`, then `direct.appender = CapturingAppender`. On Darwin, oshai memoizes each `KLogger` at **creation** time: a logger created before the `loggerFactory` swap is a `DarwinKLogger` that writes straight to os_log and can never be re-routed through the appender (it doesn't read `direct.appender` at log time; `DirectKLogger` does). Consumers call `installLogCapture` deferred (e.g. inside `scope.launch`, after a disk `recover()`), so kuilt's top-level `private val logger`s (`SeamRoom`, `JoinerResumeMachine`, `HeartbeatPartitionDetector`, `RaftEngine`, `SeamElectionLobby`) — the exact stack that spins up to establish a session — memoize as `DarwinKLogger` first and are lost.

## Fix
Decouple the **factory flip** (must happen synchronously, as early as possible) from the **appender swap** (can stay async, since `DirectKLogger` late-binds the appender at log time). Expose a tiny synchronous `installLoggerFactory()` in `kuilt-otel-logging` that a consumer calls at process entry, before any kuilt construction — and

title: kuilt-session: adopt-path resume — <15s blip loops to HostLost(Refused) instead of resuming
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Part of #1618. Found in the Fable review of PR #1632.

**A joiner whose link blips for less than the host's 15 s liveness timeout never resumes** — it burns
its 60 s reconnect budget and dies with `HostLost(Refused)`.

## The loop

Verified against `main` on 2026-07-26:

1. The joiner's device path drops. `NwSeam`'s 10 s `wovenPathGrace` expires, it evicts the host
   locally and re-forms `Woven`; its detector reports `TransportClosed` → `attemptReconnect`.
2. **The host's link to the joiner never closed** — only the joiner's side tore — so the host's
   `collectIncoming` never completes and never fires the immediate `TransportClosed`.
3. The joiner sends `AdmitMessage.Resume`. In `HeartbeatPartitionDetector.collectIncoming` **any**
   inbound frame calls `observedPeer(peerId)`, refreshing `lastSeenEpochMs`.
4. So the host's silence never reaches `HeartbeatConfig.timeout`, `onPeerUnresponsive` never fires,
   `windows[peerId]` stays `null`, and `tryResume` returns `WindowNotYetOpen` — **retryable**.
5. The joiner sleeps `heartbeatConfig.interval` and retries, refreshing `lastSeen` again. Goto 3,
   until the 60 s `reconnectWindow` elapses → `FailureReason.Refused` → `HostLost`.

**The fix cannot go host-side.** At the instant a `Resume` arrives the host cannot distinguish this
from the #1572 fast-reconnect race — in both, the roster still shows the peer `Connected`. The
discriminator is only available **over time, on the joiner**: a `WindowNotYetOpen` that persists
beyond the host's own timeout proves no window is coming.

## Status — fix LANDED; what remains is deployment + hardware validation

Implemented in [`20d27aaa`](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/commit/20d27aaa) (#1848), first
shipped in snapshot

title: kuilt-nw/session: dead peer lingers in seam.peers ~213s (no fast eviction) — wedges elections
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Part of #1618 (the deeper metronome) and related to the kuilt-nw fabric epic #1403.

A real remote airplane-mode drop produces no fast NW signal: no close is sent, the local path stays `ready` (so `PathLost`/`wovenPathGrace` — a *local* signal — never arms), and `NwConnState.Closed` arrives only when TCP gives up (~213s, the "Operation timed out" in the #1618 evidence). So the dead peer **stays in `seam.peers` for minutes**. Consequences: the surviving peer's detector fires `Timeout` (not `TransportClosed`); and the election layer keeps re-seating the zombie (matches "38 present-but-unreachable host", ~20s re-elect cadence) — arguably the true metronome of #1618's churn.

Design options to evaluate (needs-design): heartbeat-driven eviction feedback from `HeartbeatPartitionDetector`/session into the seam's peer set (a `PeerLost` prunes `seam.peers`, converting the episode to `TransportClosed`); or NW keepalive tuning so a remote drop closes faster; or filtering `electHost`'s input by liveness instead of mutating `seam.peers` at all. Where the eviction authority lives (fabric vs session) is the decision.

title: kuilt-session: route a joiner's host Timeout into attemptReconnect (not just TransportClosed)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Part of #1618. Complement to the adopt-path resume fix (PR #1632).

`SeamRoom.handleUnresponsive` routes a joiner's host-loss to `resumeMachine.attemptReconnect` **only** on `PartitionEvent.Reason.TransportClosed`. A `Timeout` (host silent but still in `seam.peers`) goes to `markPartitioned` → no `WindowOpened` (no `reconnectController` on a joiner) → `PeerLost` → terminal `HostLost` at ~75s, **never entering the reweave/resume loop**.

On a real remote airplane drop the host lingers in `seam.peers` for ~213s (NW gives no fast signal), so the **Timeout lane is the dominant one** — and #1632 doesn't touch it. The resume loop already degrades gracefully while the host is silently present in `peers` (it waits for `Woven` and retries), so routing the joiner-host `Timeout` into `attemptReconnect` (or otherwise opening a joiner-side window on that path) is the natural extension.

Gated on the 2-phone capture confirming `reason=Timeout branch=markPartitioned` (diagnostics in #1628/#1634).

title: log capture: attributeMapper resolves on the drain coroutine, so records queued across a state change get the wrong attributes
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Sibling of #1034, which fixed the same class of bug for **trace context**. `LogCapture.resolveTrace` is now resolved at the synchronous log edge, but `CaptureConfig.attributeMapper` is still resolved on the **drain** coroutine.

## Why it matters
A consumer that maps ambient state into attributes gets that state as of **drain time**, not **emit time**. Any record still queued when the ambient state changes is stamped with the *new* value — silently mis-attributed, with no way for the consumer to detect it.

Concretely, in `tractat-us/fireworks-compose` (ADR-073, tractat-us/fireworks-compose#3767): we stamp `game.id` / `session.id` onto `LogRecord`s while a server-mediated game is active. Records emitted near the end of game A but drained after game B is armed take **B's** `game.id`. That corrupts exactly the artifact the feature exists to produce — a per-game interleaved timeline used to debug reconnect failures, where the boundary records are the interesting ones.

We've documented the caveat and structured our tests to drain per phase rather than hide it, but the boundary records are genuinely mis-stamped and no consumer-side workaround can fix it — the emit-time value is gone by the time the mapper runs.

## Suggested fix
Mirror what #1034 did for trace: resolve attributes at the synchronous log edge and carry the resolved values on the queued record, or expose an edge-resolved attribute hook alongside `resolveTrace` so consumers can opt into emit-time semantics.

## Repro sketch
1. Configure a `CaptureConfig.attributeMapper` reading a mutable ambient holder.
2. Emit a record with the holder set to A.
3. Change the holder to B **before** the drain runs.
4. Observe the record carries B.

title: heddle — coordinate-generic SchedulingPolicy: unify fair-share + placement (north star)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Someday / needs-design — not v1.** Scheduling is one operation: `select = argmin over { c : feasible(c) } of (weight(c)·coord(c), tieBreakId(c))`. EEVDF fair-share is that functor with **coord = virtual service time** (feasible = `v ≤ V`, weight = share); locality placement is the same functor with **coord = distance** (feasible = capability match, weight = affinity). The weighted-fair-queueing ↔ weighted-rendezvous-hashing correspondence is real.

So the two 'pluggable' axes — ranking *policy* and *eligibility/placement* — are the **same axis**. A future `SchedulingPolicy` could be generic over a `Coordinate<C>` (`position`/`feasible`/`weight`), with EEVDF and locality placement as two instances, and Model A's affinity-as-a-*score* becoming a coordinate position.

v1 keeps EEVDF (§7) and Model A (#1625) concrete — premature generality is its own trap. This issue records the unification as the principled north star. See design §14.6.

Part of #1602.

title: heddle — Model B: conserved spatial entitlement (cpuset analogue, north star)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Someday / needs-design — not v1.** The mirror of entitlement across the time↔space duality (design §14.6). Heddle conserves a *temporal* budget (service units along a virtual timeline). **Model B conserves a *spatial* budget** — a group/lane bound to a location set, whose entitlement only *exists*/is spendable at eligible peers (a tenant's GPU-budget that lives only on GPU nodes). This is the **cpuset analogue** (a cgroup bound to a CPU set) — and algebraically it is *the heddle ledger with the axis relabelled*.

Deferred because it couples locality into the conserved lineage and inherits the partition subtleties: a spatial budget on a location set that vanishes is stranded-and-unusable (arguably correct, needs care). Distinct from Model A (#1625 — pure eligibility, no budget, safe/additive).

Part of #1602.

title: heddle H8 — location eligibility & affinity (Model A: can-I-execute-here)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

**Phase 8 of #1602** (blocked on H6; may overlap H7). "Can I execute *here*" — a placement-side eligibility overlay. Design [§14.6](https://github.com/tractat-us/kuilt/blob/main/docs/heddle-design.md). Lands in `:kuilt-warp` + `:kuilt-warp-heddle`.

**Orthogonal to the ledger** — introduces no conserved quantity, so conservation is untouched. Work:
- Peer **capabilities** as soft state: `EphemeralMap<PeerId, CapSet>` (same shape as demand §6), each peer advertises its own slot.
- A task **affinity predicate** riding the opaque envelope as a `.where { }` `Draft` modifier (`warp.shuttle(work).where { it.has(GPU) && it.region == "us-east" }.lane("acme/gpu").weave()`).
- Placement consistent-hashes over the **eligible subset** of the roster — a warp-core ring change needing no `:kuilt-heddle` type (eligibility is independent of entitlement); composes with lanes.

**Acceptance:** eligible set bit-identical across peers from the same convergent capability view; no landing on an ineligible peer under a fresh view; stale-view misplacement absorbed by `Results` dedup + ring re-home (no double-apply, no lost task); zero effect on the ledger's invariants; the no-affinity default reproduces today's placement bit-for-bit.

Part of #1602.

title: kuilt-nw: WindowOpened is delivered intermittently on a peer drop — the Timeout/markPartitioned branch can reach eviction without ever publishing a window
body:
> 🤖 This comment was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Summary — **corrected 2026-07-26: intermittent, not absent**

On **kuilt-nw** (Network.framework mesh), a real Wi-Fi drop of a peer emits `MembershipEvent.WindowOpened` on the host's `Room.events` **only sometimes**. Instrumented capture on 2026-07-24 (pin `0.7.0-dev.939`) proved the event *does* reach a host consumer — the original "`Room.events` is silent" framing below was wrong, and is retained only as the first capture.

The defect is **unreliable delivery**, which is harder for consumers than absence: a consumer cannot tell "no window opened" from "window event lost", so a drop resolves correctly on one attempt and hangs forever on the next.

### The corrected evidence (2-iPhone sustained airplane drop, dev.939)

Two drops the same night, same build, same pair of devices:

- **Drop A — event fired.** Full pipeline observed host-side: `raw Partitioned(TransportClosed) → NoChange`, `raw WindowOpened(expiresAt) → Emit`, presence applied `Paused(expiresAt)`, then on expiry `windowExpired.evict(PartitionExpired)` → `Left(PartitionExpired)` → peer detached → `Departed`. Reason cycled `TransportClosed → LinkTimeout` under heavy AWDL flapping (see #1660).
- **Drop B — no event.** `membership.unresponsive reason=Timeout branch=markPartitioned` → **no `WindowOpened`, no presence emit** → `windowExpired.evict reason=PartitionExpired` → `adapter.left`. The consumer stayed `Paused` with no terminal; the surviving device's screen froze.

So the `Timeout`/`markPartitioned` branch appears to reach eviction **without** opening (or without publishing) the window that the `TransportClosed` branch does. That asymmetry is the suspected locus.

body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

> ## ✅ Spike complete — Outcome B. Do not re-run it.
>
> **Result: `sec_protocol_options_add_pre_shared_key` is TLS 1.2-only. A 1.3 floor is unsupported by this API.** The spike's stated premise below — *"this is a bug in our wiring, not an Apple limitation"* — was **disproven**, and so was its leading SHA-384 suspect (restricting to SHA-256-only suites produces an identical failure).
>
> Proven against the real `macosArm64` 127.0.0.1 loopback handshake (macOS 26.5.2 build 25F84, Xcode SDK MacOSX26.5, K/N 2.3.21), instrumenting negotiated version + suite on both ends across 4 configs:
>
> - The working PSK link negotiates `0x00A8 = TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` — a dedicated **RFC 4279 (TLS 1.2)** PSK ciphersuite with **no TLS 1.3 analogue**.
> - Pinning `min = 1.3` fails `-9858 errSSLHandshakeFail` with `negotiated = none`: the handshake never reaches suite selection, because the PSK is never presented as a 1.3 `pre_shared_key`.

title: kuilt-session: predicate/unbounded reconnect-window hold (injectable JoinerReconnectController)
body:
> 🤖 This issue was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Gap

`DefaultJoinerReconnectController` (`kuilt-session .../partition/DefaultJoinerReconnectController.kt`) holds a **fixed** `reconnectWindowMs` — `expiresAt = at + reconnectWindowMs`, a bounded timer. It can be *refreshed* (`onPeerUnresponsive` re-arms) and *force-expired early* (`expire(peerId, at)`), but there is:

- **no unbounded / externally-driven / predicate expiry mode**, and
- **no injection seam** — `SeamRoom` constructs the controller **internally** (`SeamRoom.kt:521-523`), so a host application cannot substitute its own hold policy or drive `expire()` from an application predicate.

## Why we need it (fireworks Track 4 / rejoinable games, tractat-us/fireworks-compose#3637)

We want a seat to be held **while a durable `ResumableGame` record exists** — a *predicate*, not a fixed timeout. A player who force-quits and comes back 10 minutes later should still reclaim their seat, because the durable record says the game is theirs to rejoin; the current fixed `reconnectWindow` expires the hold long before that.

Today fireworks works around the absence of this by keeping its *own* second window (a `graceWindowMs` timer in `LiveLeaderImpl` / `LiveSeatTracker`). That duplicate window is exactly what fireworks#3634 / #3647 are retiring so kuilt is the single authority — but we can only fully retire it once kuilt can express the predicate/unbounded hold. Per our clean-room + "a gap in kuilt is a kuilt issue, never a fireworks workaround" rule, this is a kuilt feature, not a fireworks timer.

## Requested shape (either is fine — your call)

1. **Injectable controller** — let a `SeamRoom` host pass a `JoinerReconnectController` (interface) instead of always constructing `DefaultJoinerReconnectController`
